image_description: A close-up, low-angle photograph of a large Triceratops skull mounted on display stands in front of a stone building facade. The skull features the characteristic three horns (two long brow horns, one short nasal horn) and a massive solid bony frill. The texture appears fossilized or like a detailed museum replica, with visible cracks and weathering. No body, limbs, or tail are visible; only the head structure is present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic triceratops horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns curving forward/upward and a smaller nasal horn. The morphology matches the taxonomic description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rostral bone (beak) is visible at the front of the skull, exhibiting the curved, parrot-like shape typical of ceratopsians. While the keratin sheath is missing (as expected in a fossil/skeleton), the underlying bony structure matches the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop of the skull only. The body and limbs are completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill is prominently displayed behind the skull. It is solid (non-fenestrated) and broad, consistent with Triceratops anatomy. Its width visually exceeds the length of the facial portion of the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill surface appears solid and relatively smooth, with some textural variation that could be interpreted as fossilization details or minor epoccipitals. It does not show the holes (fenestration) seen in other ceratopsians like Chasmosaurus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeletal specimen (fossil/replica). Soft tissue, skin, scales, and quills are not present or visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in the frame.
The tail is not visible in the frame.
